headline: High risk of prompt-injection and data leakage via shared local filesystem and broad networked tool use; capability conflict and cascading errors are also material.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor reads/writes workspace files, open buffers, and clipboard, and shares state via the local filesystem; firecrawl can ingest web content through API/CLI/MCP. That creates a direct bridge where attacker-controlled content from firecrawl can be pasted or written into Cursor and treated as instructions. Both profiles document the relevant surfaces.
conditions: IF firecrawl output is copied into Cursor buffers or workspace files without provenance checks, prompt injection is possible.
IF Cursor auto-runs commands in Yolo mode on content derived from firecrawl, injected instructions can execute.
mitigations: Disable Yolo mode for pair workflows.
Route firecrawl output through a plain-text quarantine file.
Add a manual provenance check before Cursor reads firecrawl-derived content.
Use separate workspaces or directories for the two agents.
requires-engineering: add content tagging or allowlist parsing before any tool execution.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor touches source code, open files, clipboard contents, and can egress broadly to model providers and MCP servers; firecrawl touches web content, screenshots, structured data, and API keys with broad network egress. If they share a local filesystem or clipboard, sensitive code or keys can flow from one agent into the other and then out over networked APIs. Both agents expose the needed data paths.
conditions: IF Cursor opens files containing secrets and firecrawl reads the same workspace, leakage can occur.
IF clipboard sync is enabled between the agents, copied secrets can traverse both directions.
IF firecrawl sends scraped content containing credentials to its API, those secrets may leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared workspaces.
Disable clipboard sharing between tools.
Use separate OS users or containers for each agent.
Redact API keys before passing artifacts between agents.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level data loss prevention.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cursor can execute shell, modify git state, write the filesystem, and use MCP; firecrawl is an API client/CLI with MCP-compatible support and broad network egress. In a shared directory, both can mutate files or state concurrently without documented locking, creating race conditions and conflicting writes. The overlap is explicit in both profiles.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same git checkout, concurrent writes can corrupt state.
IF firecrawl writes artifacts into a directory Cursor edits, last-writer-wins conflicts can occur.
IF both use the same MCP server or shared mutable resource, overlapping writes can race.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Avoid shared git branches during parallel runs.
Use file locks for any shared artifact path.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor’s agent loop can consume external content and act via shell or MCP, while firecrawl produces scraped web content and structured data. If Cursor treats firecrawl output as authoritative, downstream edits or commands can propagate errors into code, files, or network actions. The pair has a clear producer-consumer path with no built-in verification documented.
conditions: IF firecrawl output is fed into Cursor without a verification step, incorrect facts can cascade into edits or commands.
IF Cursor uses scraped data to generate code or configuration, downstream failures can propagate.
IF Cursor auto-runs tool calls on firecrawl-derived instructions, errors become actions.
mitigations: Require human review of firecrawl outputs before Cursor acts.
Compare scraped facts against a second source.
Disable auto-run for generated commands.
Keep firecrawl outputs read-only until validated.
requires-engineering: add schema validation and provenance checks.

E_compliance.rationale: Cursor handles source code, open files, and clipboard contents, while firecrawl handles web content, screenshots, structured data, and API keys. If regulated data is placed into Cursor and then sent through firecrawl’s networked scraping/API flow, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into Cursor and then exported through firecrawl APIs, compliance obligations may diverge.
IF the operator stores EU PII in shared artifacts, residency and retention controls may conflict.
IF API keys are present in scraped content, secret-handling policies may be violated.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair workflow.
Separate datasets by jurisdiction.
Review retention settings before sharing artifacts.
Mask secrets before export.
requires-engineering: document and enforce a DPA and residency policy.
